title: Italy: Thieves steal key Renaissance paintings in Sicily
facts: Robbers broke into the Regional Museum of Messina in Sicily on August 15, 2026.
The burglary at the Regional Museum of Messina occurred around 10:00 p.m. local time.
Thieves stole several painted panels created by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina.
Three of the five surviving panels from Antonello da Messina's 1473 'San Gregorio Polyptych' were stolen.
A small double-sided panel locked inside an armored display case was stolen during the robbery.
Marisa Mercurio serves as the director of the Regional Museum of Messina.
Federico Basile serves as the mayor of Messina.
Initial estimates value the stolen Antonello da Messina artworks between 70 million and 80 million euros.
The Italian state purchased a panel painted by Antonello da Messina around 1460 for $14.9 million in March 2026.
Antonello da Messina was born around 1430 and worked in Messina until his death in 1474.
An earthquake in Messina on December 28, 1908, destroyed most of the city's cultural heritage.
The thieves left two stolen painted panels leaning against the exterior of the museum building.
Italian authorities recently recovered three stolen artworks by Auguste Renoir, Paul Cezanne, and Henri Matisse worth about 10 million euros.
The artworks by Renoir, Cezanne, and Matisse were stolen from the Magnani Rocca Foundation in Parma on March 22.
Five individuals were detained in connection with the theft from the Magnani Rocca Foundation.
